text: If the legal entity is the "who," the ledger is the "book." This lesson covers the three kinds of ledger Oracle Fusion supports, and the four defining characteristics every ledger needs.

Every ledger is defined by its chart of accounts, calendar, currency, and subledger accounting method — the ledger's four C's. Two ledgers sharing all four are candidates for a ledger set; differ in even one and they're accounting for things differently.

The primary ledger is the mandatory, central record-keeping ledger. Every accounting configuration is built around exactly one, directly linked to subledger transactions from Payables, Receivables, and the rest.

A secondary ledger is optional and tied to a primary ledger — it maintains an alternative accounting representation, maybe a different GAAP or chart of accounts. A reporting currency is simpler: the same ledger, restated in another currency.
Primary ledger: mandatory and central. Secondary ledger: an alternate accounting representation. Reporting currency: the same book, translated. Next up, lesson eight: ledger sets.
